items.markdown:
The UAE is rolling out its national **e-invoicing system** (E-Billing / e-Invoicing framework) using a decentralized **5-corner model** built on the **Peppol network** and **PINT-AE** specifications.[[1]](https://edicomgroup.com/blog/united-arab-emirates-electronic-invoicing-project)

To comply with the mandates—which begin rolling out for large taxpayers (revenue ≥ AED 50M) and scale broadly—businesses must integrate through official **Accredited Service Providers (ASPs)** and certified Peppol Access Points.[[1]](https://edicomgroup.com/blog/united-arab-emirates-electronic-invoicing-project)

### Understanding the Provider Ecosystem

- **Accredited Service Providers (ASPs):** The UAE Ministry of Finance (MoF) and the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) oversee a growing roster of officially approved and pre-approved ASPs.[[1]](https://finline.ae/en/articles/uae-e-invoicing-asp-list)
- **Peppol Access Point (AP) Certification:** Authorized providers must hold active certified Peppol access point status to handle network-level document signing, secure routing, and direct tax data reporting to the FTA.[[1]](https://edicomgroup.com/blog/united-arab-emirates-electronic-invoicing-project)
- **Notable Market Players:** International and regional enterprise solution providers have secured early official accreditations (such as **EDICOM** , alongside a growing list of over 50+ approved and pre-approved software vendors and tech partners).[[1]](https://edicomgroup.com/blog/united-arab-emirates-electronic-invoicing-project)[[2]](https://finline.ae/en/articles/uae-e-invoicing-asp-list)

### What to Look for When Choosing a Provider

When selecting an e-invoicing service provider for your business, verify the following core capabilities:

1. **Official Accreditation Status:** Confirm that the vendor is listed on the official Ministry of Finance / FTA accredited ASP registry rather than relying on generic claims.[[1]](https://www.citytechme.com/insights/e-invoicing-service-providers-uae/)
2. **Peppol & PINT-AE Compliance:** Ensure the provider natively supports the Peppol transport layer and the specific UAE PINT-AE invoice structure/format requirements.[[1]](https://edicomgroup.com/blog/united-arab-emirates-electronic-invoicing-project)[[2]](https://www.citytechme.com/insights/e-invoicing-service-providers-uae/)
3. **ERP & Accounting Integration:** Check seamless connectivity with your existing infrastructure (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics 365, or custom legacy billing software).[[1]](https://www.citytechme.com/insights/e-invoicing-service-providers-uae/)
4. **Security & Data Residency:** Verify that the provider meets strict data encryption, multi-factor authentication, and local data protection standards.[[1]](https://www.flick.network/en-ae/uae-e-invoicing-accreditation)

You can track active updates, announcements, and compliance guidelines directly through the [Federal Tax Authority - UAE E-Invoicing Portal](https://tax.gov.ae/en/content/uae.einvoicing.aspx).[[1]](https://tax.gov.ae/en/content/uae.einvoicing.aspx)

If you'd like, let me know:

- Your **annual revenue bracket** (to see when the mandate applies to your business)
- Your **current accounting or ERP software** (SAP, Oracle, Zoho, etc.)

I can help you narrow down the best integration path or check specific provider readiness.
